section.title: 短文 3
section.preview: Women continue to spend more time than men taking care of children and doing chores around the house.

lines.text: Women continue to spend more time than men taking care of children and doing chores around the house.
This is generally attributed to backward thinking and conservative values.
But new research shows that such differences could be linked to differences in the preferences of males and females.
The new study looked at how men and women were dividing work at home and why they divided it that way.
In general, both men and women took more responsibility for tasks they liked.
For example, men liked yard care and home maintenance more than women.
They leaned toward wanting primary responsibility for such tasks.
The researchers stated that differences in enjoyment of household and childcare tasks matched how men and women chose to split tasks.
The researchers added that there was not a single childcare task that men liked more than women.
Keep in mind, however, that as with any research on group differences, there were large within-group differences.
The study's authors concluded that differences in men's and women's time spent on childcare and household tasks do not mean dissatisfaction.
The authors noted that previous research revealed gender differences in attitudes towards family and career.
These differences appear as early as 6 years old.
Girls that age already show more interest in helping and caring for others than boys do.
And they already exhibit a greater orientation toward family versus career.
